theme: Controversies; new wineskins; the true family of Jesus
readingInstruction: Read Mark 2:1-3:35. A paralyzed man is lowered through a roof, Jesus eats with sinners, the Sabbath controversies begin, and opposition hardens. Notice who Jesus welcomes and who rejects him.
settingTheScene: These two chapters contain a series of five conflict stories in Galilee. In each, the religious leaders challenge Jesus’ authority: to forgive sins, to eat with sinners, to set aside fasting, and to interpret the Sabbath. By the end of chapter 3, the Pharisees are plotting with the Herodians to destroy him. Mark places the opposition early to show that the road to the cross begins here.
observation: “But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” (2:10).
“Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners” (2:17).
“And no one puts new wine into old wineskins” (2:22).
“The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath” (2:27).
“And he looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart” (3:5).
“Whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of an eternal sin” (3:29).
“For whoever does the will of God, he is my brother and sister and mother” (3:35).
interpretation:
Four friends bring a paralyzed man to Jesus, and when they cannot get through the crowd, they dig through the roof. Jesus sees their faith and says to the man, “Son, your sins are forgiven.” The scribes think, “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” They are right about the principle, and that is the point. Jesus then heals the man to prove that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins. The man’s greatest need was forgiveness, and Jesus addressed that first.

He calls Levi, a tax collector, and eats with tax collectors and sinners. When the scribes complain, he says, “Those who are well have no need of a physician.” He has come for the sick. Anyone who thinks they are well will miss him.

When asked why his disciples do not fast, he says the bridegroom is with them. A wedding is no time for fasting. The old way and the new cannot be patched together: new wine requires new wineskins. The new covenant does not fit into the old forms. This is a key statement of the discontinuity in the covenants. What Jesus brings is new.

The Sabbath conflicts follow. His disciples pick grain on the Sabbath, and Jesus says, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath. So the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.” In the synagogue he heals a man with a withered hand, and asks whether it is lawful to do good or harm on the Sabbath. They are silent. He looks at them with anger, “grieved at their hardness of heart.” Jesus is angry and sad at the same time. The Pharisees go out and plot with the Herodians how to destroy him.

In chapter 3, crowds follow him, and he appoints twelve to be with him and to be sent out. His family thinks he is out of his mind. The scribes from Jerusalem say he casts out demons by Beelzebul. Jesus responds that a house divided cannot stand, and warns that to attribute the Spirit’s work to Satan is an unforgivable blasphemy, a settled refusal to see God’s work as good. Finally, when his mother and brothers arrive, he looks at those sitting around him and says, “Here are my mother and my brothers! Whoever does the will of God, he is my brother and sister and mother.” The new family of God is defined by obedience to him.
connection: Isaiah 43:25 says God alone blots out transgressions. Psalm 103:3 says the LORD forgives all your iniquity. Hosea 6:6 is the mercy-over-sacrifice theme. 1 Samuel 21:1-6 is David and the bread. Exodus 20:8-11 and Deuteronomy 5:12-15 are the Sabbath commands. Jeremiah 31:31-34 promised a new covenant. Hebrews 8:13 says the first covenant is becoming obsolete. Galatians 3:26-29 and Ephesians 2:19 describe the new family of God.
application:
Think of those who brought you to Jesus. Thank God for them, and ask whom you could carry to him.

Reflect on whether you are a patient who needs the physician. Admit your need.

Ask what “doing the will of God” looks like in your family and church this week.
prayerPrompts: Thank Jesus for authority to forgive sins, and for forgiving yours.
Thank him for coming for sinners.
Ask him to make you new wine, ready for what he is doing.
